title: [Fix] tensor_bridge: preserve lazy CPU view values when importing into MLX
body:
## Motivation

CPU Torch tensors can carry lazy conjugate or negative bits. Importing their physical storage directly into MLX loses those logical transformations, so a conjugated complex tensor or the imaginary view of a conjugate can produce incorrect values through `torch_to_mlx`, `mlx_call`, and `mlx_call_multi`.

## Modifications

Resolve conjugate and negative bits after detaching the CPU tensor and before creating the owning MLX array. Ordinary tensors retain the existing path. The MPS borrowing path, CPU float64 handling, complex128 rejection, source ownership, and gradient-detachment contract remain unchanged.

Add seven tests for conjugate/negative/scalar/empty/noncontiguous views, source flags and gradients, independent output storage, and the public bridge call helpers.

## Accuracy Tests

Exact-source native validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/sglang/actions/runs/43399327572

- Native MLX 0.32.4 and PyTorch 2.14.1 on Linux CPU; the test asserts that the checkout's bridge is imported and no CUDA/MPS device is available.
- Complete bridge module: **13 tests passed, 11 subtests passed, 26 MPS-only tests skipped**.
- Restoring the original source produces **2 failing test methods and 5 failing subtests**, with 11 completed methods, 6 passing subtests and the same 26 skips. Failures compare logical tensor values, not imports or unavailable devices.
- Repository pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

This validates the CPU conversion path. Apple MPS borrowing and end-to-end model generation were not exercised.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput improvement is claimed. Resolving a lazy view may materialize its logical values before the existing owning MLX copy; this is necessary for correct conversion.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with repository pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add unit tests in the existing registered bridge test module.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- Documentation: no public API change.
- Accuracy: native tensor-value and bridge-call checks above; no model benchmark claim.
